interpretation_boundary.benchmark_abstraction: a positive evidence graph whose untyped baseline erases token/request coordinates
interpretation_boundary.normative_claim: the registered validation facts must be checked as properties of the presented token/proof context
not_claimed: that a compliant OAuth implementation normally unions arbitrary token claims
that the synthetic corpus measures real-world vulnerability prevalence
that the encoding has received independent OAuth working-group adjudication

registered_requirements: access tokens can be audience-restricted to a protected resource
a token intended for one protected resource must not be treated as valid at another
scope describes what access is granted while resource/audience identifies where it can be redeemed
sources.title: Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0

registered_requirements: JWT access tokens are explicitly typed and signed
issuer, expiration, audience, subject, client, issue time, and token identifier are token-associated claims
scope strings must have meaning for the resources in the token audience
a resource server must exactly validate issuer and expected audience and reject a mismatching token
authorization claims are used together with the validated token context
cross-JWT confusion and ambiguous grants must be prevented
sources.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens

registered_requirements: a resource server verifies that the DPoP proof key matches the key bound to the access token
the ath claim must match the presented access token
method and target URI checks belong to the same proof used for the request
access must not be granted unless all DPoP checks succeed
sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP)

registered_requirements: access tokens should be restricted to intended resources and actions
resource servers verify that the presented token is meant for the requested resource and action
sender-constrained tokens are recommended where appropriate to reduce replay
sources.title: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
